population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: of the 27.9 on in 2032, 57% (15.9) stayed on, down from 60% because of employer retreat and the Bridge lapse, and 12.0 stopped. The off pool was 9.1 + 12.0 = 21.1, of whom 55% (11.6) restarted, leaving 9.5 off. New ever-users added 4.8 pts: 3.7 on and 1.1 already off. On = 15.9 + 11.6 + 3.7 = 31.2. Off = 9.5 + 1.1 = 10.6 = ever 41.8 − current 31.2. Cycled = 13.4 (by 2032) + 5.4 first-time restarters (the other 6.2 of the 11.6 restarters had cycled before) + 0.3 among new starters = 19.1 of 41.8 = 46%. Current users ≈ 84.2M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 3.40 + 11.22 + 12.24 + 4.37 = 31.2. Income thirds: (40 + 31 + 22.6)/3 = 31.2. The top–bottom gap widened from 12.3 to 17.4 pts: top-third users kept employer coverage longest and can afford retatrutide cash plus coaching, while the bottom third is held near 22.6% by flat HRSA funding and Medicaid lockouts. The middle rose 28→31 almost entirely through $199 TrumpRx cash purchases after employers dropped coverage. 50–64 reached 51%, driven by 'brain health' and cash semaglutide. 65+ rose only 17→19% (~11.8M) because the Medicare Bridge lapsed on 31 Dec 2033. Of its 3.4M users, ~1.5M were re-coded into Part D under cardiovascular, dementia-risk, OSA or CKD labels, ~1.0M moved to cash, ~0.2M to gray product, and ~0.7M stopped and now sit in the off pool. Off-drug: ~28.6M adults have used and stopped. Many were cut off involuntarily, by Medicaid lockouts, by the loss of employer weight-only coverage, or by the Bridge lapse. ~157M have never used. They include the organised refusers, the uninsured in non-expansion states, people with contraindications and a growing group of low-income adults priced out at $199. Pediatric: 1.3% of ~73M ≈ 950k, ~160k of them aged 6–11, with growth slowed because employer weight-only coverage of dependents fell with adult coverage. Children whose parents switched from covered to cash drug are the newest family pattern: one pen in the fridge, rationed between two adults.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge lapsed on 31 Dec 2033 when the year-end health-extenders package omitted it, and it has not been revived. Medicare still pays for incretins coded for type 2 diabetes, established cardiovascular disease (SELECT label), dementia-risk reduction in eligible adults ≥55 with CVD, OSA and CKD. That is ≈12.6% of fills ≈ 10.6M users (7.6M previously coded + 1.5M re-coded from the Bridge + 1.5M new diabetes and dementia-label starts) at an average net ≈$215/month: 10.6M × $215 × 12 ≈ $27.3B/yr. The Bridge's DEXA and resistance-training conditions lapsed with it. Coded Part D users carry only the label's Warnings-section DEXA recommendation. Medicaid pays ≈11.2% ≈ 9.4M users at ≈$215: 9.4M × $215 × 12 ≈ $24.3B/yr combined federal and state, with the same seven adherence waivers (IN, AR, MO, OK, GA, OH, MT). The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program has been held at $5.0B under full-year continuing resolutions in FY2033 and FY2034, still unconditional, and now runs waitlists. It serves ≈3.8M: 2.5M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $2.1B, plus 1.3M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $169 × 12 = $2.6B, ≈ $4.7B. TRICARE, the VA and the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program cover ≈2.6M, including ~165k active-duty members: 165k × $149 × 12 ≈ $295M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 90+ semaglutide brands at $6–35/month and generic tirzepatide is sold in India, Brazil, Turkey, Egypt and Indonesia. Generic semaglutide is standard across Canada, Mexico, China and most of Latin America and Asia. Chinese triple agonists are approved domestically and exported to ASEAN and Gulf markets. In the US, the 2033 settlement entry dates passed, but by the end of 2034 FDA had granted only tentative approvals to semaglutide ANDAs, and the settlements key entry to final approval. Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~84.2M users: commercial 28.3% (23.8M: ~15.0M on diabetes/cardiac/OSA codes, ~8.8M weight-only, mostly at large employers in finance, tech, health systems and the public sector), Medicare 12.6% (10.6M), Medicaid 11.2% (9.4M), HRSA 4.5% (3.8M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.1% (2.6M), cash/direct 28.0% (23.6M), gray 12.4% (10.4M) = 100%. The cash/direct share doubled from 11.1M as employer and Bridge coverage receded. Household out-of-pocket ≈ 23.6M × ~$200 average × 12 ≈ $57B/yr. Managed decline continued: from Jan 2034 the Strategic Supply Agreement stepped TrumpRx/direct prices to $199 (semaglutide injection), $249 (tirzepatide), $299 (retatrutide) and $149 (oral starts, unchanged). MariTide sells mostly through coverage at a $399 direct price. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Employer weight-management coverage fell from 63% to 44% for plan year 2034. The Aug 2033 Third Circuit ruling barred PBM adherence data as a wellness 'reasonable alternative standard' within that circuit and chilled premium differentials elsewhere, and many employers chose exclusion over unconditioned coverage. Only ~20% of remaining covering employers still attach conditions, mostly coaching enrollment rather than PDC. Skip-but-fill fell sharply in commercial plans but persists in the seven Medicaid waiver states. Gray users rose from ~9.0M to ~10.4M despite Section 232 seizures: 503A compounders at $89–179 absorbed people dropped by employers who could not reach $199.

GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 small-molecule, daily oral (orforglipron: Foundayo; low-dose BED presentation)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)
GLP-1 agonist / GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, obesity with MASH F2–F3)

reduction in risk of dementia in adults ≥55 with type 2 diabetes or obesity plus established cardiovascular disease (semaglutide, Jun 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet mind' low-dose Foundayo after a brief telehealth BED screen, ~1.5M users on the BED presentation, many of them screen-positive at the margin
'brain health' semaglutide for 50–64-year-olds outside the dementia label, now mostly cash-paid at $199
semaglutide for ages 6–11 under pediatric endocrinology
gambling, compulsive shopping and cannabis reduction, still without a label
antiresorptive 'bone cover' co-prescribing in 65+, guideline-endorsed, though uptake fell among former Bridge users now on cash
'household split' dosing, in which couples on one cash pen stretch doses, against labelling
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached the US market and no new indication was approved this step. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (BLA Mar 2032) received a complete response letter in May 2033. FDA asked for functional-outcome and fracture data rather than lean-mass surrogates, and a resubmission is expected no earlier than 2035. Amycretin received a CRL in Sep 2033 over fill-finish observations at a contract site and a request for longer pancreatic-safety follow-up; Novo plans to resubmit in 2035. MariTide supply expanded to ~1.8M users as Amgen's Ohio capacity came online. Survodutide stays narrow. US incretin revenue growth slowed: volume +13% over the window, net price −10 to −12%. The global market is ≈$178B in 2034, with ex-US volume growth carried largely by Indian and Chinese generics outside originator revenue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are higher on retatrutide 12 mg, among gray users who skip titration, and among cash users who stretch doses and re-titrate erratically.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: MDL 3094 has ~70,000 filed and tolled claims. Bellwether results remain split, and court-ordered mediation began in 2034 without a global settlement. Persistence after stopping is still disputed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Reserves raised again in 2033 annual reports.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide 12 mg volume and rapid loss.
Low absolute risk, no causal confirmation. FDA's request for longer pancreatic follow-up for amycretin keeps the question open.

The population problem persists. It is now socially patterned: worst among cash and HRSA users without coaching or protein support, and least among covered users with trainers. The Bridge's resistance-training referral ended with the lapse.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings section unchanged. The bimagrumab combination got a CRL in May 2033 for lacking functional outcomes. HRSA still has no muscle requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose a further ~3% in 2032–33, then flattened in 2034 as DEXA and antiresorptive uptake spread among covered users. Excess is modelled at ≈ 11.8M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr × HR ~0.30 ≈ 18,000/yr, still concentrated in women and cyclers, with a new concern about ~1.0M former Bridge users now on cash without mandated DEXA. The final adolescent registry analysis (2034) adjudicated a lumbar-spine BMD z-score accrual deficit of ~0.15 SD after >3 years. Part of it is attributed to weight loss itself.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric labelling updated in the Use in Specific Populations section (2034) to recommend DEXA in adolescents on drug >2 years. Adult Warnings unchanged. The Bridge DEXA mandate lapsed with the programme.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the BED and AUD populations and in the pooled anhedonia analysis.

FDA's pooled analysis of 38 randomised trials (Feb 2033) found a clinically meaningful SHAPS shift in ~4.6% on drug vs ~1.9% on placebo, about 3 attributable cases per 100, dose-dependent and highest on retatrutide ≥8 mg (~8% vs ~4%). Long-term user surveys still report 10–15% 'reduced pleasure', a gap regulators attribute partly to caloric deficit and attribution. Deliberate dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~30% of long-term users as employer conditioning receded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling change (Feb 2033): 'Reduced pleasure (anhedonia)' is listed in Adverse Reactions for all incretins with the ~3–5% estimate, and as a Warning for retatrutide doses above 8 mg, with a recommendation to reassess or dose-reduce. The FTC continues to police 'calm/focus' claims.

safety_ledger.effect: Anhedonia in adolescents and low-dose BED users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The pooled analysis had few adolescents and few low-dose BED users on sub-maintenance doses who were not truly binge-eating. Pediatric registry mood instruments were added only in 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA postmarketing requirement for an adolescent mood study; BED labelling notes limited data in sub-threshold users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Increasingly driven by coverage loss rather than conditioning: employer weight-only exclusions for 2034, the Bridge lapse (~0.7M stopped) and Medicaid lockouts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist, concentrated in cash and HRSA users without counselling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance only, now that the Bridge counselling requirement has lapsed.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven years of adolescent follow-up. ~160k children aged 6–11 on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still inconclusive at the first interim.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; bone labelling updated 2034.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls rose ~12% over the window, mostly compounded-semaglutide dosing errors among people newly dropped by employers.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Continued CBP seizures under Section 232; ~45 further warning letters; two further distributor prosecutions, none of users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
'Brain health' use outside the label keeps growing among 50–64-year-olds, now mostly cash-paid and therefore outside any payer DEXA or counselling requirement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling states the population limits; no enforcement against off-label prescribing.

food_and_beverage.state: US packaged-food volume falls ~2% a year, slightly slower as adoption growth moderates. The sector has split by income. Premium protein, fibre and 'bone-and-muscle' lines are sold in affluent-zip grocers and through employer-covered coaching apps. Calorie-dense value packs grow in dollar stores in the neighbourhoods where coverage receded. Brands sold to private equity in 2030–32 are now run explicitly for the off-drug and never-user consumer.

alcohol.state: A fifth year of falling US spirits and beer volume, though the decline slowed to ~2% a year. Distillers report the clearest income gradient in their history: premium on-premise volume in high-income metros is down most, value beer least.

restaurants.state: Unit closures continue at mid-priced suburban chains. Value chains in lower-income markets stabilise, and some reopen dollar menus aimed at non-users. Upscale venues sell 'protein-forward' small plates at full price. 'Open Table' church suppers persist with no measurable sales effect.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. Fit language now carries class: 'athletic cut' and tailored muscle fits are priced and marketed to the trained-on-drug, while 'relaxed' and plus lines sit with value retailers. Alteration services in Charlotte and Austin grow on cash customers who are losing weight. Uniform makers re-cut for military and police again.

fitness.state: Premium strength studios and private trainers grow fast in affluent metros as the class marker becomes muscle on drug. Low-cost PT chains and Medicare Advantage strength programmes lost a referral stream when the Bridge lapsed, and some Sun City gym waiting lists cleared. Net growth, but bifurcated.

insurance.state: Employer pharmacy trend fell to ~+4% as weight-only coverage was dropped and net prices fell. Plans concentrate incretin spend on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and CKD codes. Carve-out vendors sell 'cardiometabolic-only' benefit designs, and coding for SELECT-label eligibility has become a utilisation-review battleground. PBM adherence-verification revenue shrank after the Third Circuit ruling.

pharma.state: Lilly remains the national champion and federal price setter, with cash-channel volume replacing lost employer volume at lower margin. Novo secured partial duty relief through a Strategic Supply addendum tied to its Clayton, NC API expansion, but its margin is still compressed. Semaglutide ANDA holders wait on final FDA approval. The 503A compounders gained customers, while API costs stay high under Chinese amino-acid controls. MDL reserves keep rising.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now reads as a benefits package. Visible muscle on a lean frame says covered and coached: a weight-only employer plan, a trainer, DEXA on file. A lean but soft 'pen-thin' frame says cash, $199 a month and no one supervising it. A heavier body increasingly says the plan dropped you or the price was one bill too many. The refuser identity still exists, but it now has to compete with the plainer reading that you are poor.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Columbus, Ohio, hourly warehouse and retail workers whose employers dropped weight-only coverage for 2034 are the clearest case. A distribution-centre floor that was visibly leaner in 2032 now shows three bodies by shift and pay grade: supervisors on covered retatrutide with gym stipends, line staff splitting cash semaglutide or buying compounded vials, and recent hires never on. Recruiters for client-facing roles in Columbus and Charlotte quietly treat the 'Charlotte build' as a soft credential. The phrase 'plan body' has entered speech for a muscled, drug-lean physique.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Eating has become a class marker. In affluent households a small, high-protein plate is the norm, and full family dinners are for holidays. In households that lost coverage, meals swing with the pen: lean months and full months. 'Open Table' suppers continue in Grand Rapids, Nashville and Tulsa, and now draw more people who were dropped from coverage than people who refused it.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added 'build' filters in 2033, and users read them as income proxies. 'Covered' appears in profiles the way 'homeowner' once did. Couples on one cash budget negotiate who gets the pen this quarter.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is no longer contractual for most commercial users now that conditioning has largely gone, but it is priced. Being hungry means you are not paying. The backlash language of 'hunger is how we were made' persists but sounds different when the hungry are mostly the uncovered. Tennessee's and Idaho's 'appetite liberty' laws remain, though they matter less with fewer conditioned plans.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The Feb 2033 class label put attributable clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~3 per 100 (4.6% vs 1.9%), with ~8% vs ~4% on high-dose retatrutide. Clinics now screen with a brief SHAPS at dose changes. Surveys still find 10–15% of long-term users reporting 'reduced pleasure', but the published figure governs the conversation. Deliberate dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~30% of long-term users, and commercial skip-but-fill largely ended with conditioning. Low-dose Foundayo BED users ≈1.5M. Telehealth 'quiet' subscriptions are down to ~0.9M.
interior_life.framing: A side effect with a number. 'The grey' survives as slang among long-term users, but most people, clinicians included, now say 'the anhedonia thing, the four percent'. Pharmacists ask about it at dose changes as they ask about nausea. Late-night comedy moved on. The BED advertising ('quiet the noise around food') continues and carries the new label language in its fine print.
interior_life.effect_on_work: With premium conditioning mostly gone, mood and adherence have left the workplace as variables. Employers no longer track fills, and sales staff no longer time holidays to quarter-end. Occupational-health clinics in police and military programmes added a SHAPS item at annual review after the label change. Chaplains still hear 'the grey', less often.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billing has faded to a niche at a few festivals. Comedy about the grey is now nostalgia material. Casino and betting operators stopped citing incretins as a headwind in 2034 calls, attributing flat handle to the broader user base rather than to new users.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use the label section as a screening prompt rather than a cultural reference. Dose holidays around conception and anniversaries continue but are discussed as medical decisions. For cash couples the argument is about whose turn it is with the pen, not about flatness.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash coalition lost its most vivid grievance when 'chemical contentment' became a small labelled number. Its centre of gravity moved to class and access, opposing the readiness programme while arguing over the Bridge lapse. Pro-access populists campaign on restoring the Bridge and on TrumpRx prices. Candidates are still asked whether they are on, and the follow-up is now 'who pays?'

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and labelling-led, with no new programmes or mandates this step. FDA approved no new indication or class, issued CRLs for bimagrumab + tirzepatide and amycretin, and acted on anhedonia and pediatric bone through labelling.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. The Medicare Bridge lapsed on 31 Dec 2033. HRSA is held at $5.0B under full-year CRs, unconditional, with waitlists. The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program and the ACA cessation mandate (two 90-day courses a year) continue unchanged. The Strategic Supply Agreement price steps continued under existing terms.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Employer conditioning has largely collapsed. The Third Circuit (Aug 2033) held that PBM adherence data are not a reasonable alternative standard under the wellness rules, and employers elsewhere retreated rather than risk suits. The seven Medicaid adherence waivers remain the main surviving conditioned channel, so skip-but-fill is now concentrated among the poorest users. The Bridge's DEXA and response conditions ended with it.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program covers ~165k active-duty members, and body-composition separations stay ~30% below the 2030 baseline. Religious-accommodation requests total ~2,600. Phoenix, Houston and Chicago police and fire contracts continue, and the FAA special-issuance pathway is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 duties on incretin API and peptide intermediates continue, and Lilly remains the tariff-exempt national champion. A WTO panel on India's complaint was established in Jul 2033, and its report is due in 2035. Commerce's 2033 ruling that the duties apply to imported API for ANDA products leaves Indian-sourced generic semaglutide uncompetitive even once approved. Novo's Clayton API addendum gives it partial relief. Chinese amino-acid export controls remain.

events.event: FDA orders class labelling for all incretins listing 'reduced pleasure (anhedonia)' as an adverse reaction in about 3–5% of patients, based on a pooled analysis of 38 trials, with a Warning for retatrutide above 8 mg; pharmacies begin a two-question screen at dose changes

FDA rejects Lilly's bimagrumab–tirzepatide combination, asking for fracture and physical-function outcomes rather than lean-mass scans; in September Novo's amycretin also receives a complete response letter over fill-finish observations

WTO establishes a panel on India's challenge to US incretin duties; Commerce rules the Section 232 tariffs apply to imported API in generic semaglutide as the 2033 settlement entry dates pass with only tentative FDA approvals

Third Circuit rules that employers cannot base wellness premium differentials on PBM adherence data; within weeks large employers announce they will drop weight-only GLP-1 coverage for 2034 and cover only diabetes, cardiac, apnea and kidney codes, and surveys later show employer coverage down from 63% to 44%

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge expires when Congress's year-end health-extenders package omits it; about 1.5 million of its 3.4 million users are re-coded under cardiovascular and dementia-risk labels, and the rest move to cash, compounders, or off the drug

TrumpRx steps down under the Strategic Supply Agreement to $199 for semaglutide, $249 for tirzepatide and $299 for retatrutide, with oral starts held at $149; Novo matches after a supply addendum tied to its North Carolina API plant grants partial duty relief

open_tensions: The Bridge lapse moved about a million older adults onto cash drug just as their bone and muscle safeguards (DEXA, training referrals, protein counselling) disappeared. Fracture data for 2035 will show whether the 2034 flattening was real. Restoring the Bridge is now a campaign issue with no bill moving.

Two tiers have hardened. Coverage follows diabetes and cardiac codes and high-wage employers, while 23.6M people pay about $57B a year out of pocket and 10.4M use compounders. The body has become a visible income signal, and the bottom third is held at 22.6% by a flat HRSA budget and Medicaid lockouts.

The national-champion bargain is under strain. Semaglutide ANDAs await final approval, Section 232 duties make Indian-sourced generics uneconomic, and the WTO panel reports in 2035. A loss at the WTO, or an FDA final approval, could break the managed price ladder from below.

The class label calls anhedonia a ~3% attributable effect, but long-term users report 10–15%, and adolescents and sub-threshold BED users were barely studied. The 'niche' framing rests on a number the mood studies of 2035–36 may revise.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: The Plan Body: Employers walked away, the pen got cheaper, and now you can read an American's paycheck from across the room
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 a little under a third of American adults, about eighty-four million people, take an incretin drug. The number still rises, but more slowly than it did, and who pays for it has changed. Two years ago coverage came with conditions: weigh-ins, adherence feeds, premium differentials. Most of those conditions are gone now, and much of the coverage went with them.

The turn came in a courtroom. In September 2033 the Third Circuit ruled that employers could not set premiums using the pharmacy data that showed whether workers filled their pens. Offered a choice between paying for the drug with no conditions and not paying for it, many employers chose not to pay. For the 2034 plan year, more than half the companies that had covered weight loss stopped. They kept paying for diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea and kidney disease. Coding for a heart indication became the new fight with utilisation review. Fewer than half of employers now cover the drug for weight alone, and the ones that do are mostly banks, hospitals, tech firms and public agencies.

Three months later the Medicare Bridge expired quietly. Congress's year-end package left it out, and nobody fought to put it back in time. About half its users were re-coded under the heart and dementia labels. The rest pay cash, buy from compounders or have stopped. The bone-scan and strength-training conditions that came with the Bridge ended too, and endocrinologists are waiting to see what the 2035 fracture numbers show.

The cash price has made up most of the difference. The federal portal now sells semaglutide at $199 a month, tirzepatide at $249 and the triple agonist at $299, and Novo matched after a deal over its North Carolina plant. Almost twenty-four million Americans pay out of pocket, close to sixty billion dollars a year, money that used to go on groceries, drinks and dinners out. Another ten million buy compounded vials for less. Generic semaglutide was supposed to arrive in 2033. It has tentative approvals and a tariff waiting for it, and India's complaint about that tariff now sits before a WTO panel.

The result is a body that can be read by price. In Columbus, Ohio, the floor of a distribution centre that dropped coverage in January shows it plainly. Supervisors with covered retatrutide and a gym stipend have what people call a plan body: lean and visibly trained. Line workers who split a cash pen at home are thinner but soft, which trainers still call pen-thin. New hires who never started look like the country did ten years ago. Recruiters for client-facing jobs do not say they notice, and dating apps added a 'build' filter that everyone reads as an income filter. Grocers in affluent zip codes sell protein-forward food and smaller portions. Dollar stores sell more of the value packs the big food companies offloaded years ago.

The grey has shrunk. In February 2033 the FDA put reduced pleasure on the label of every incretin with an estimate of about three extra cases per hundred, more at high triple-agonist doses. A number turned a mood into a side effect. Pharmacists now ask two screening questions at dose changes, and comedians have dropped the subject. Long-term users still tell surveys more often than that about a flatness, but the published figure is the one that gets quoted.

Nothing new reached the market. The FDA rejected both the muscle-sparing combination and the amylin hybrid. The Pentagon's programme continues, and the free clinics run waitlists on a frozen budget. From the outside the country looks fitter at the top and about the same at the bottom.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renée Okafor clocks in at 5:50 at the Groveport distribution centre outside Columbus. The pen is in the butter compartment at home. Tuesday is her week.

At break the vending machine has the new value packs, two cookies the size of saucers. She doesn't want one, which is the point of the pen, and she paid $199 for that point on the first of the month. Her husband Dele's Mounjaro is coded for his diabetes and costs twenty-five dollars. Hers was weight-only, and the plan stopped covering it in January.

Her shift lead, Brandon, has forearms like a man in an advertisement. His company card pays for a trainer. He's on the triple. Everyone knows, and nobody says it.

At lunch her sister texts a photo of a vial from a compounder in Dayton: $119, a different shape of number. Renée deletes it, then fishes it out of the trash folder.

At four she stops at the Kroger on Hamilton Road for chicken thighs, the cheap protein. Her son Tobi, eleven, wants the cereal with the cartoon tiger. She buys it. He eats like a boy, and she likes watching him do it.

At nine Dele lays the pen on the counter beside the leaflet. The new line is underlined in someone else's pen, from the pharmacy: reduced pleasure, about three to five in a hundred.

'You feel it?' he asks.

She thinks about the cereal, Tobi's spoon and the tiger.

'No,' she says. She pinches her stomach and injects.

least_plausible_claims.quote: For the 2034 plan year, more than half the companies that had covered weight loss stopped.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude and mechanism. The world state has employer coverage falling from 63% to 44%, a drop of about 30% in relative terms, so 'more than half' contradicts the candidate's own figure.
